source.title: Add "Database Migration" section (Debezium CDC) under Guides & References / Databases
source.body:
## Summary

This issue adds a new sub-section **"Database Migration"** under **Guides & References / Databases**
(`modules/ROOT/pages/database/migration/`). It teaches how to migrate a database from a legacy system to a new one
**without a big-bang cut-over**, by using **[Debezium](https://debezium.io/)** to turn every committed change in the
legacy database into an event, publishing those events to a message broker (Apache Kafka by default), and listening to
them to keep the new database (and new services) in sync while both systems run side by side.

The sub-section covers **every concept in the official Debezium documentation** (architecture, features, installation,
every source and sink connector, change-event format, serialization, snapshots, signaling, notifications,
transformations, post processors, Debezium Server, Debezium Engine, the Operator and the Management Platform,
integrations, monitoring, operations and the FAQ). Each concept is explained from the migration point of view: how it helps
**generate change events**, **listen to them**, and **use them to migrate a database**.

It builds on, and links to, the architecture pages that already describe the patterns. It does not repeat them:
* `backend/architecture/decisions-and-migrations/migration-overview.adoc`: no big bang, strangler fig, demonstrate value early
* `backend/architecture/decisions-and-migrations/migration-path-legacy-to-modern-stack.adoc`: the Bookshop Oracle →
  PostgreSQL strangler migration, the anti-corruption layer, and "Data synchronisation during the overlap" (dual writes vs CDC)
* `backend/architecture/decisions-and-migrations/migration-path-monolith-to-microservices.adoc`: "How the monolith
  publishes domain events" (publishing at each write site vs transaction-log tailing/CDC)
* `backend/architecture/architectural-patterns/transactional-outbox.adoc`: the polling publisher vs transaction-log tailing
* `backend/architecture/architectural-patterns/listen-to-yourself.adoc`, `cqrs.adoc`, `event-sourcing.adoc`, `sagas.adoc`
* `backend/messaging/kafka-connect.adoc`, `kafka-serialization-and-schemas.adoc`,
  `kafka-reliability-and-exactly-once.adoc`, `messaging-patterns-in-practice.adoc`, `spring-boot-kafka.adoc`
* `database/schema-evolution/*` (Liquibase / Flamingock, expand/contract)
* `database/choosing-the-right-database.adoc` ("Keeping Several Databases Consistent -- CQRS")

Those pages say *that* CDC with Debezium is the safer default for keeping a legacy and a new database in sync. This
sub-section explains *how* to do it, end to end, with working configuration and code.

## Original request

> Explore official documentation about Debezium (a tool to listen to database changes) to learn how to use it. Then
> update github issue 382 to include a new section called "Database Migration" within "Guides & References" /
> "Databases". For each explored concept in the official documentation of Debezium, updated github issue must indicate
> to create a detailed documentation pages to teach how to use Debezium to generate events and listen to them in order
> to be able to migrate a database. Take into account architecture documentation pages in this repository, as they
> probably also explain concepts and patterns to migrate systems and databases and keep legacy and new systems both in
> sync using messaging queues and tools like debezium. Each detailed page indicated to be created must contain detailed
> information and code examples linked to the official documentation. Mermaid diagrams and figures in SVG format can be
> added if they help to understand concepts. A bibliography section must be added listing all sources used to generate
> this documentation about Debezium. Each source must be linked to its official website. Admonitions must only indicate
> that documentation was generated with AI assistance. A cheat sheet page must be added containing a one page
> downloadable PDF summarizing all generated documentation about debezium.

The issue was created with only the title "Debezium: database migration from legacy systems". The requested scope was added on 2026-11-09.

## Placement and navigation

* Directory: `modules/ROOT/pages/database/migration/`. Nav title: **"Database Migration"**.
* Nav: a new `*** xref:database/migration/index.adoc[Database Migration]` block in `modules/ROOT/nav.adoc`, placed
  **directly after the "Evolving the Database Model" block** (after `schema-evolution/best-practices.adoc`) and before
  `** xref:web/index.adoc[Web Development]`. Pages are `****` entries. The groups in the outline are shown as
  `****` plain-text group headings with `*****` page entries, as other large sections do. A flat list with
  `Group: Title` prefixes is also acceptable.
* `database/index.adoc`: add a bullet for the new sub-section (after "Evolving the Database Model") and mention it in the
  page's `:description:`.
* Page attributes: every page has `:description:` and `:keywords:`, a "checked on 2026-MM-DD against Debezium 3.7.x"
  line, and `include::partial$database-migration-disclaimer.adoc[]` right after the header.

## Version baseline (verified 2026-11-09)

* **Debezium 3.7.1.Final** (released 2026-11-06; 3.7 GA was announced 2026-09-29). Official docs use the
  `https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/` URLs, which serve 3.7. When a page depends on a specific version,
  also link the pinned `/reference/3.7/` URL.
* Debezium **3.8** is in development (3.8.0.Alpha1, 2026-11-02, adds an Elasticsearch sink). Mention it only as
  "upcoming", and add no 3.8-only configuration.
* Java **17+** for connectors. Java **21+** for Debezium Server, the Operator, the Outbox Quarkus extension and the Quarkus
  Debezium engine extension.
* Kafka Connect **3.1+**. The `quay.io/debezium/{kafka,connect,server,operator,example-mysql,example-postgres}:3.7.1.Final` images
  ship Kafka 4.x (KRaft, no ZooKeeper).
* Tested database versions for 3.7, from https://debezium.io/releases/3.7/: MySQL 8.0/8.4/9.7, MariaDB
  11.4/11.8/12.3, PostgreSQL 14–18, Oracle 19c/21c/23ai/26ai, SQL Server 2017/2019/2022, MongoDB 6.0/7.0/8.0, Db2
  11.5, Informix 12/14/15, Cassandra 4/5 and others. Pages must copy the table from the releases page, not from memory.
* Running applications: Spring Boot 4.1 + Spring for Apache Kafka (same baseline as the architecture pages). Quarkus is shown
  where Debezium has a Quarkus extension.

### Facts the implementer must not get wrong (removed or renamed in recent releases)
* `topic.prefix` replaced `database.server.name`. `schema.history.internal.*` replaced `database.history.*`.
* `snapshot.mode=schema_only` is deprecated in favour of `no_data`, and `schema_only_recovery` in favour of `recovery`.
* `ExtractNewRecordState` uses `delete.tombstone.handling.mode` (`drop`, `tombstone`, `rewrite`,
  `rewrite-with-tombstone`, `delete-to-tombstone`). `drop.tombstones` and `delete.handling.mode` are gone.
* MongoDB: `mongodb.connection.string` replaced `mongodb.hosts`. A standalone server is not supported (it must be a
  replica set or a sharded cluster).
* Oracle: `log.mining.strategy=redo_log_catalog` is deprecated (use `hybrid`). Continuous mining (12c) was removed in 3.7.
  Adapters: `logminer` (default), `logminer_unbuffered`, `olr` (OpenLogReplicator), `xstream` (needs a GoldenGate licence).
* 3.7 removed the Cassandra 3 connector. The old Debezium UI is superseded by the **Debezium Management Platform** (do not
  document the UI).
* 3.7 JDBC sink: `schema.evolution=validate-only` is new, and MySQL → MySQL type handling changed (`BIGINT UNSIGNED`, `BIT`,
  `ENUM`/`SET`, `TIME`).
* Incubating connectors (Vitess, Spanner, Informix, YashanDB, Ingres, Milvus, and Db2 for IBM i, SQLite and TiDB from
  the databases page) must be labelled as incubating.

## Running example

The running example is **Bookshop**, the same example as the architecture pages: the legacy Java EE/Struts application
on a **monolithic Oracle schema** (`BOOKSHOP` schema: `BOOK`, `AUTHOR`, `CUSTOMER`, `ORDERS`, `ORDER_LINE`,
`SUPPLIER_CATALOGUE`, all upper-case table-per-column naming, numeric flags, `NUMBER` keys, `DATE` columns), migrated by
strangler fig to the new **Spring Boot 4.1 `bookshop` application on PostgreSQL 18** with a different model
(`book`, `author`, `book_author`, `customer`, `purchase_order`, `order_line`, snake_case, `uuid`/`bigint` keys,
`timestamptz`, `numeric(12,2)`).

* Quick-start and connector labs use small local stacks (MySQL or PostgreSQL in Docker Compose) so readers can run them
  in minutes. The Oracle labs use the `gvenzl/oracle-free` image (Oracle Database 23ai Free) and are marked as heavier.
* A secondary MongoDB example (legacy `bookshop.reviews` collection → PostgreSQL table, and the reverse) shows the
  document ↔ relational cases.
* Every compose file, connector JSON, Kubernetes manifest and Java class must be complete enough to copy and run.
  Every one ends with a `Source:` / `Reference:` link to the official page and anchor it is derived from.

## Content conventions (apply to every page)

1. **Detailed, teaching prose.** Each page explains what the concept is, why it matters for migration, how to configure
   it, what can go wrong, and how to verify it. Pages are not summaries of the official docs.
2. **Code examples linked to the official documentation.** Every connector config, SMT config, signal SQL, compose
   file, Kubernetes CR and Java/Quarkus snippet is followed by a link to the exact official page and anchor (for example
   `https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/postgresql.html#postgresql-connector-properties`).
3. **Mermaid diagrams** (sequence, flowchart, state) where they help. Follow `CLAUDE.md` § Mermaid diagrams: write
   any `<` that is followed by a letter as an entity, and run `npm run validate:mermaid`.
4. **SVG figures** in `modules/ROOT/images/` named `database-migration-*.svg`. Each figure is referenced by at least one
   page. Image macros are on one line, and alt text that contains commas is quoted (`CLAUDE.md` § Images and figures).
   Planned figures are listed in the outline. Each SVG needs a light background or theme-safe colours.
5. **Admonitions: only one kind, the AI-assistance notice.** The new partial
   `modules/ROOT/partials/database-migration-disclaimer.adoc` contains a single `[IMPORTANT]` block. The block says
   that the content was generated with AI assistance and must be checked against the official Debezium documentation,
   and links to the bibliography. **No other admonition (`NOTE`, `TIP`, `WARNING`, `CAUTION`, `IMPORTANT`) may be used
   anywhere in the sub-section.** Warnings and tips are written as normal prose, as lists or as table rows.
6. **Inline code** follows `CLAUDE.md` § Inline code: write `+...+` passthroughs for values such as
   `+${routedByValue}+`, `+${source.table}+`, `+->+`, and use `pass:c[...]` for values that contain `+`.
7. **Cross-links instead of duplication.** Kafka, Kafka Connect, Strimzi, Spring Kafka, the outbox, CQRS, the strangler fig
   and the anti-corruption layer are explained on their existing pages, so link them. The new pages explain only what
   is specific to Debezium and to database migration.
8. **No prices.** Managed-service references (Amazon MSK Connect, Confluent Cloud, Red Hat build of Debezium) describe
   capabilities only, with a checked-on date.

## Existing pages to update (small cross-link edits only)

* `backend/architecture/decisions-and-migrations/migration-path-legacy-to-modern-stack.adoc`, § "Data synchronisation
  during the overlap": add one sentence linking to `database/migration/index.adoc` and the worked example.
* `backend/architecture/decisions-and-migrations/migration-path-monolith-to-microservices.adoc`, § "How the monolith
  publishes domain events": link to the CDC source-connector pages.
* `backend/architecture/architectural-patterns/transactional-outbox.adoc`, § "Transaction-log tailing / CDC": link to
  `database/migration/outbox-event-router.adoc`.
* `backend/messaging/kafka-connect.adoc` and `backend/messaging/messaging-patterns-in-practice.adoc`: link to the new
  sub-section. Bump their pinned `reference/3.6/` Debezium URLs to `stable` or `3.7`.
* `backend/architecture/decisions-and-migrations/index.adoc` and `database/choosing-the-right-database.adoc`: add a
  "see also" link.
* `database/index.adoc` and `nav.adoc`, as described above.

## Bibliography (index page, `== Bibliography`)

The index page ends with a `== Bibliography` section that lists **every source used to write the sub-section**. Each entry
links to the source's official website. At least these sources are expected; the implementer adds anything else they
consult:

**Debezium (official)**

* [debezium/container-images (GitHub)](https://github.com/debezium/container-images) and the
  [quay.io/debezium](https://quay.io/organization/debezium) images
* [Debezium 3.7.0.Final release announcement](https://debezium.io/blog/2026/09/29/debezium-3-7-final-released/)

  [Outbox Quarkus extension](https://debezium.io/blog/2020/01/22/outbox-quarkus-extension/),
  [Event sourcing vs CDC](https://debezium.io/blog/2020/02/10/event-sourcing-vs-cdc/),

Before the bibliography is published, open every URL in it to check that it still resolves.

## Cheat sheet

`database/migration/cheat-sheet.adoc` is a page with a single-page, colour-coded summary of the whole sub-section and
`xref:attachment$database-migration-cheat-sheet.pdf[Download the Database Migration (Debezium) Cheat Sheet (PDF)]`. The PDF
in `modules/ROOT/attachments/` is **one A4/Letter landscape page** and is generated from the cheat-sheet content. Its
contents are in the outline comment, page 44.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `database/migration/` contains the 44 pages in the outline comments, with nav entries and an index page that
      describes reading paths (for example "new to CDC", "migrating Oracle → PostgreSQL", "operating Debezium").
- [ ] Every concept in the official Debezium 3.7 documentation nav is covered by at least one page (the coverage
      table in comment 2 maps each official page to a new page).
- [ ] Every page has detailed prose and runnable code/config examples, and each example links to its official doc.
- [ ] Mermaid diagrams pass `npm run validate:mermaid`. Each SVG in `images/` is referenced and renders, and the
      `CLAUDE.md` image and inline-code checks print nothing.
- [ ] The partial AI-assistance notice is the only admonition in the sub-section
      (`grep -rnE '^\[(NOTE|TIP|WARNING|CAUTION|IMPORTANT)\]|^(NOTE|TIP|WARNING|CAUTION|IMPORTANT):' modules/ROOT/pages/database/migration`
      prints nothing).
- [ ] The bibliography lists every source used, each linked to its official website.
- [ ] The cheat sheet page and the one-page PDF exist, and the PDF downloads from the built site.
- [ ] The existing architecture and messaging pages link to the new sub-section.
- [ ] `npx antora antora-playbook.yml` builds with no xref or AsciiDoc errors.

The page outline is in the two comments below. It does not fit in the issue body.

comments.text:
## Page outline, part 1 of 2 (pages 1–22)

`B` = `https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable`. Each page lists the official pages it is based on, and its
code examples link to the anchors shown. "Fig" = SVG in `images/`, "Mermaid" = inline diagram.

### Introduction

1. **`index.adoc` — Database Migration.** What the sub-section covers and who it is for. The problem: a legacy database
   that must keep running while a new system takes over. Why log-based CDC is the core technique (summary + links to the
   architecture pages). Reading paths. Version baseline table. The Bookshop running example (legacy Oracle schema vs the
   new PostgreSQL model, side-by-side table). Page map grouped as in the nav. **`== Bibliography`** (see issue body).
   Fig: `database-migration-overview.svg` (legacy app + Oracle → Debezium → Kafka → consumers/JDBC sink → PostgreSQL + new
   app, with the strangler proxy in front). Sources: `B/index.html`, https://debezium.io/why/use-cases/.
2. **`migration-strategies.adoc` — Migration Strategies: Big Bang, Dual Writes, Batch ETL and CDC.** Compares big-bang
   dump/restore, application dual writes, batch ETL, trigger-based capture, query-based (polling `updated_at`) capture
   and log-based CDC. For each: consistency, deletes, latency, load on the legacy DB, and code changes needed in the
   legacy app. Decision table. Explains why log-based CDC sees deletes and intermediate states that polling misses.
   Links `migration-overview.adoc`, `migration-path-legacy-to-modern-stack.adoc#_data_synchronisation_during_the_overlap`
   and `transactional-outbox.adoc`. Mermaid: the dual-write failure sequence vs the CDC sequence. Sources:
   https://debezium.io/documentation/faq/, the "Streaming to another database" blog post, and microservices.io transaction log tailing.
3. **`migration-patterns-with-cdc.adoc` — Migration Patterns with CDC.** The phases of a CDC-driven migration:
   (1) initial snapshot + streaming into the new store, (2) parallel run and reconciliation, (3) read cut-over,
   (4) write cut-over with reverse replication for rollback, (5) decommission. Strangler fig at the data layer (linked to
   the Grahsl/Morling talk). The anti-corruption layer as a stream translator. Expand/contract on the new schema (links
   `schema-evolution`). CDC feeding CQRS read models (links `cqrs.adoc`). Outbox vs raw table CDC (domain events vs
   row changes, and when to use each). Fig: `database-migration-phases.svg` (timeline of the five phases, showing which
   system is the source of truth). Mermaid: state diagram of the migration phases with the rollback transitions.

### Debezium fundamentals

4. **`debezium-architecture.adoc` — Debezium Architecture.** The three ways to run it: Kafka Connect (source connectors
   in a Connect cluster), Debezium Server (standalone, with Kafka-less sinks) and the Debezium Engine (embedded library).
   Covers how a connector reads the log, offsets, the schema history topic, and topics per table (`topic.prefix`.schema.table).
   Explains which option suits a migration (Kafka Connect for a long, many-consumer strangler; Server/JDBC sink for
   point-to-point replication; Engine for an in-process pipeline). Fig: `database-migration-debezium-deployment-options.svg`.
   Source: `B/architecture.html`.
5. **`debezium-features-and-guarantees.adoc` — Features and Delivery Guarantees.** Snapshots followed by streaming, no lost
   changes, deletes, old row images, transaction metadata (`provide.transaction.metadata`, the transaction topic, BEGIN/END
   events), at-least-once delivery and how consumers deduplicate, per-key ordering, and the exactly-once support
   (`B/configuration/eos.html`) with its requirements. Mermaid: a sequence showing a restart and the redelivery window.
   Sources: `B/features.html`, `B/configuration/eos.html`.
6. **`getting-started-tutorial.adoc` — Getting Started: Your First Change Events.** The official Kafka Connect tutorial,
   rebuilt as a Docker Compose file with `quay.io/debezium/kafka:3.7.1.Final`, `connect:3.7.1.Final` and
   `example-mysql:3.7.1.Final`. Register the MySQL connector with `curl` against the Connect REST API. Watch events with
   `kafka-console-consumer` / `kcat`. Insert, update and delete rows and read the resulting events. Restart the connector
   and see that it resumes from its offset. Clean up. Also shows the same lab with `example-postgres`. Source:
   `B/kc-tutorial.html` (#starting-services, #deploying-mysql-connector, #viewing-change-events, #cleaning-up),
   `B/tutorials.html`.
7. **`installation-and-deployment.adoc` — Installing Debezium.** The install options: container images, connector plugin
   archives in the Connect `plugin.path`, Maven artifacts (`io.debezium:debezium-connector-*`), a custom Connect image
   with a Dockerfile, the Strimzi `build` section (only summarised here, with the details on page 35), and the Debezium
   CLI. Covers Java baselines, Kafka Connect worker configuration (`group.id`, `config/offset/status.storage.topic`,
   converters, `config.providers` for secrets) and checking the plugin with `GET /connector-plugins`. Sources:
   `B/install.html`, `B/install-kafka-connect.html`, https://debezium.io/installation/kafka-connect/, the Debezium
   CLI blog post.

### Change events

8. **`change-event-structure.adoc` — Anatomy of a Change Event.** Covers the key (primary key, or
   `message.key.columns` when the table has none) and the value envelope: `before`, `after`, `source`, `op` (`c`, `u`,
   `d`, `r`, `t`, `m`), `ts_ms`/`ts_us`/`ts_ns`, `transaction`. Explains delete events followed by tombstones
   (`tombstones.on.delete`), primary key updates (a delete + create pair), `schemas.enable` in the JSON converter, and how
   `source.ts_ms` differs from `ts_ms` (this is how lag is measured). Gives one annotated real example for a Bookshop
   `BOOK` update and one for a delete. Fig: `database-migration-change-event-anatomy.svg`. Sources: `#postgresql-events`,
   `#mysql-events`, `#oracle-events`, `#mysql-tombstone-events`.
9. **`serialization-avro-and-schema-registries.adoc` — Serialization: JSON, Avro, Schema Registries and CloudEvents.**
   Covers the JSON converter with and without schemas, Avro with Apicurio Registry (with the Debezium container setup) and
   with Confluent Schema Registry, Avro naming rules, the Debezium SerDes for Kafka Streams / plain consumers, the
   CloudEvents converter, and how schema compatibility settings interact with schema changes in the legacy DB. Sources:
   `B/configuration/avro.html` (#apicurio-registry, #deploying-with-debezium-containers, #confluent-schema-registry,
   #avro-naming), `B/integrations/serdes.html`, `B/integrations/cloudevents.html`. Links
   `backend/messaging/kafka-serialization-and-schemas.adoc`.
10. **`data-types-and-precision.adoc` — Data Types, Temporal and Decimal Precision.** The data-type mapping problems that
    break migrations. `decimal.handling.mode` (`precise`/`double`/`string`) and money columns. `time.precision.mode`
    (`adaptive`, `adaptive_time_microseconds`, `connect`, `isostring` where supported). Time zones and the
    `TimezoneConverter` SMT. `binary.handling.mode`. Oracle `NUMBER` without scale, `DATE`, `CLOB`/`BLOB` (`lob.enabled`) and
    unavailable-value placeholders (`unavailable.value.placeholder`). PostgreSQL TOASTed columns and `REPLICA IDENTITY
    FULL`. MySQL `TINYINT(1)` and `ENUM`. `column.propagate.source.type` so that the JDBC sink keeps the exact type. Gives a
    mapping table from the Bookshop Oracle columns to the PostgreSQL target types. Sources: the "Data type mappings" section
    of each connector page and `B/transformations/timezone-converter.html`.

### Source connectors (generating events)

Every connector page has: how the connector works, DB-side prerequisites (with SQL), a least-privilege user, a full
connector JSON, snapshot modes, the key properties table, connector-specific events, managed-cloud variants (RDS/Aurora,
Cloud SQL, Azure), monitoring metrics, and the "when things go wrong" items. Each one links to its official page.

11. **`oracle-connector.adoc` — Oracle Connector (the Legacy Source).** The main source in the Bookshop example. Covers
    ARCHIVELOG mode, database and per-table supplemental logging, the LogMiner user and its grants (CDB/PDB), the
    adapters (`logminer`, `logminer_unbuffered`, `olr`, `xstream`) and when to use each, mining strategies (`online_catalog`
    default, `hybrid`, `dictionary_from_file` for a standby; `redo_log_catalog` is deprecated), event buffering (heap,
    Infinispan, Ehcache), archive log destinations, long-running transactions and `log.mining.transaction.retention.ms`,
    LOB handling, RAC, and the FAQ items. Lab: `gvenzl/oracle-free` + Debezium Connect with the Oracle JDBC driver added.
    Fig: `database-migration-oracle-logminer.svg`. Source: `B/connectors/oracle.html` (#oracle-adapter-modes,
    #setting-up-oracle, #_preparing_the_database, #archive-log-destinations, #creating-users-for-the-connector,
    #oracle-logminer-mining-strategies, #oracle-event-buffering, #oracle-openlogreplicator-support,
    #oracle-xstreams-support, #oracle-connector-properties, #oracle-frequently-asked-questions).
12. **`postgresql-connector.adoc` — PostgreSQL Connector.** Covers `wal_level=logical`, `pgoutput` vs `decoderbufs`
    (and the 3.7 image change: decoderbufs is enabled, `output_plugin_libraries`), replication slots (`slot.name`,
    `slot.drop.on.stop`, failover slots on PG 17+), publications (`publication.name`,
    `publication.autocreate.mode`), `REPLICA IDENTITY`, WAL disk growth and the heartbeat fix (`heartbeat.interval.ms`,
    `heartbeat.action.query`), the replication user, and RDS/Aurora/Cloud SQL/Azure settings. Also explains the case
    where PostgreSQL is the **new** database and the source of reverse replication. Source: `B/connectors/postgresql.html`
    (#setting-up-postgresql, #postgresql-server-configuration, #_configuring_replication_slot, #postgresql-in-the-cloud,
    #postgresql-replica-identity, #postgresql-wal-disk-space, #enabling-postgresql-failover-slots,
    #postgresql-connector-properties, #postgresql-when-things-go-wrong), `B/postgres-plugins.html`.
13. **`mysql-and-mariadb-connectors.adoc` — MySQL and MariaDB Connectors.** Covers the user grants, `server-id`,
    `binlog_format=ROW`, `binlog_row_image=FULL`, an empty `binlog_row_value_options`, binlog retention, GTIDs,
    `database.server.id`, query log events, the schema history topic, the snapshot locking modes, the
    `set-binlog-position` signal, and the differences of the MariaDB connector. Source: `B/connectors/mysql.html`
    (#setting-up-mysql, #mysql-creating-user, #enable-mysql-binlog, #enable-mysql-gtids, #enable-query-log-events,
    #validate-binlog-row-value-options, #mysql-schema-history-topic, #mysql-connector-properties,
    #_setting_the_binlog_position_via_a_signal), `B/connectors/mariadb.html`.
14. **`sql-server-connector.adoc` — SQL Server Connector.** Covers `sys.sp_cdc_enable_db`, `sys.sp_cdc_enable_table`,
    SQL Server Agent, capture-job parameters, gating roles, schema changes with a new capture instance (online
    schema updates), the schema history topic, multiple databases (`database.names`), and Azure SQL / RDS. Source:
    `B/connectors/sqlserver.html` (#setting-up-sqlserver, #_enabling_cdc_on_the_sql_server_database,
    #_enabling_cdc_on_a_sql_server_table, #_sql_server_capture_job_agent_configuration_parameters,
    #sqlserver-schema-evolution, #online-schema-updates, #sqlserver-connector-properties).
15. **`mongodb-connector.adoc` — MongoDB Connector.** Covers change streams, the supported topologies (replica set or
    sharded cluster; convert a standalone server to a one-node replica set), `mongodb.connection.string`, user roles,
    `capture.mode` values and pre-images (`changeStreamPreAndPostImages`), oplog sizing, and invalid resume token
    recovery. The event format differs from the relational connectors (`after` is a JSON string). Lab: the legacy
    `bookshop.reviews` collection. Source: `B/connectors/mongodb.html` (#change-streams,
    #supported-mongodb-topologies, #required-user-permissions, #mongodb-optimal-oplog-config, #mongodb-pre-image-support,
    #mongodb-events, #mongodb-connector-properties, #connector-error-invalid-resume-token).
16. **`other-source-connectors.adoc` — Db2, Informix, Cassandra and the Other Connectors.** For each connector: what it
    captures, its main prerequisite, its maturity (stable or incubating), and when it appears in a legacy migration. Db2
    LUW/z/OS (the ASN capture tables, linking the COBOL `embedded-sql-and-db2.adoc` and `modernization-strategies.adoc`
    pages), Db2 for IBM i, Informix, Cassandra 4/5 (3 was removed), Vitess, Spanner, CockroachDB, YashanDB, Ingres,
    Milvus, SQLite, TiDB. Sources: `B/connectors/index.html`, each connector page, https://debezium.io/databases/.

### Snapshots, signals and notifications

17. **`initial-snapshots.adoc` — Initial Snapshots and Snapshot Modes.** How the initial snapshot copies the existing
    legacy data before streaming starts. Covers each `snapshot.mode` value (`initial`, `initial_only`, `no_data`,
    `when_needed`, `always`, `recovery`, `configuration_based`, `custom`; `schema_only` is deprecated), snapshot isolation
    and locking per connector (`snapshot.locking.mode`, `snapshot.isolation.mode`), `snapshot.select.statement.overrides`,
    `snapshot.max.threads`, `snapshot.fetch.size`, and sizing a multi-terabyte snapshot. Mermaid: snapshot → streaming
    hand-over at the recorded log position. Sources: `#postgresql-snapshots`, `#mysql-snapshots`, `#oracle-snapshots`.
18. **`incremental-and-blocking-snapshots.adoc` — Incremental, Read-only and Blocking Snapshots.** Ad hoc
    re-snapshots of single tables during the migration (a new table joins the scope, or a table needs to be backfilled
    again). The watermark algorithm (chunked, interleaved with streaming), `incremental.snapshot.chunk.size`,
    `additional-conditions` for partial backfills, read-only incremental snapshots (no signal table write; PG 13+, MySQL
    GTIDs), and blocking snapshots. Fig: `database-migration-incremental-snapshot-watermarks.svg`. Sources:
    `#postgresql-incremental-snapshots`, `#debezium-mysql-incremental-snapshots`, `#mysql-read-only-incremental-snapshots`,
    `#mysql-blocking-snapshots`, the incremental snapshots blog post.
19. **`signaling-and-notifications.adoc` — Signaling and Notifications.** Signal channels (`source` signal table,
    `kafka`, `jmx`, `file`, `custom`) and the `debezium_signal` table DDL. The actions: `execute-snapshot`
    (INCREMENTAL/BLOCKING), `stop-snapshot`, `pause-snapshot`, `resume-snapshot`, `log`, `set-binlog-position`, custom
    actions. Notification channels (`sink` topic, `log`, `jmx`, `custom`), initial and incremental snapshot progress
    notifications, and using them to drive a migration runbook (a script waits for "snapshot completed" before the next
    step). Code: SQL inserts, a Kafka signal message, and a Java consumer of notifications. Sources:
    `B/configuration/signalling.html` (#debezium-signaling-enabling-source-signaling-channel,
    #debezium-signaling-enabling-kafka-signaling-channel, #debezium-signaling-enabling-jmx-signaling-channel,
    #_enabling_a_file_signal_channel, #debezium-signaling-ad-hoc-incremental-snapshots,
    #debezium-signaling-stop-ad-hoc-snapshots, #debezium-signaling-pause-incremental-snapshots,
    #debezium-signaling-resume-incremental-snapshots, #debezium-signaling-ad-hoc-blocking-snapshots),
    `B/configuration/notification.html` (#debezium-notifications-about-the-status-of-an-initial-snapshot,
    #debezium-notifications-about-the-progress-of-incremental-snapshots, #enabling-debezium-notifications).

### Transformations

20. **`single-message-transformations.adoc` — Debezium Transformations.** SMT basics (linking `kafka-connect.adoc`),
    then each routing/filtering SMT applied to migration: topic routing (`ByLogicalTableRouter`, merging sharded
    legacy tables), content-based routing and filtering (with the JSR 223 / Groovy language dependency), applying
    transformations selectively (predicates), partition routing, header-to-value, the schema change event filter,
    `event-changes` (changed fields), `enforce-record-size`, geometry SMTs, TimescaleDB, logical decoding message decoding,
    vector-to-json, and the Neo4j CUD converter (each one briefly, with when it is useful). Sources:
    `B/transformations/index.html` and each transformation page.
21. **`event-flattening.adoc` — Event Flattening (New Record State Extraction).** When a consumer or a non-Debezium sink needs
    plain rows: `ExtractNewRecordState` with `add.fields` (`op`, `source.ts_ms`, `table`), `add.headers`,
    `delete.tombstone.handling.mode` (each value and its effect on the target DB), `drop.fields.*`, and
    `route.by.field`. Also covers the MongoDB event flattening and the MongoDB relational mapping SMTs for document → table
    migrations. Explains why the Debezium JDBC sink does **not** need it. Sources: `B/transformations/event-flattening.html`
    (#configuration-options), `B/transformations/mongodb-event-flattening.html`,
    `B/transformations/mongodb-relational-mapping.html`.
22. **`outbox-event-router.adoc` — Outbox Event Router.** Publishing domain events from the legacy or new application
    with CDC. Covers the outbox table layout, `EventRouter` options (`table.field.event.*`, `route.by.field`,
    `route.topic.replacement`, `table.expand.json.payload`, `table.fields.additional.placement`, Avro payloads), the
    MongoDB outbox router, and the **Outbox Quarkus extension**. A Spring Boot 4.1 outbox writer is shown and linked to the
    `transactional-outbox.adoc` page (which keeps the pattern theory). Mermaid: the outbox insert → WAL → EventRouter →
    `outbox.event.Order` topic. Sources: `B/transformations/outbox-event-router.html` (#basic-outbox-table,
    #outbox-event-router-configuration-options, #avro-as-payload-format), `B/transformations/mongodb-outbox-event-router.html`,
    `B/integrations/outbox.html`, the outbox blog post.

The outline continues in part 2.

## Page outline, part 2 of 2 (pages 23–44), coverage table

### Transformations (continued)

23. **`custom-converters-and-post-processors.adoc` — Custom Converters and Post Processors.** Writing a custom
    `CustomConverter` (Java SPI) to fix legacy column types at the source (for example Oracle `CHAR(1)` `'Y'`/`'N'` flags →
    boolean, packed `NUMBER` dates → `DATE`), with packaging and registration. Post processors: `ReselectColumnsPostProcessor`
    for unavailable LOB/TOAST values, and the S3 large-message post processor. Code: a complete Maven module +
    connector config. Sources: `B/development/converters.html`, `B/post-processors/index.html`,
    `B/post-processors/reselect-columns.html`, `B/post-processors/s3-large-message.html`.

### Listening to events and applying them to the new database

24. **`jdbc-sink-connector.adoc` — JDBC Sink Connector: Replicating into the New Database.** The main tool for
    "legacy table → new table" replication without writing code. Covers consuming native Debezium envelopes (no
    flattening), `insert.mode` (`insert`, `update`, `upsert`; use upsert for idempotent writes), `primary.key.mode` +
    `primary.key.fields`, `delete.enabled` / `truncate.enabled`, `schema.evolution` (`none`, `validate-only` new in 3.7, `basic`),
    `collection.name.format` (`+${topic}+`, `+${source.table}+`), naming strategies, `quote.identifiers`, `use.time.zone`,
    batching and the reduction buffer, PostgreSQL `unnest` inserts, SQL Server identity insert, connection pool settings,
    `hibernate.*` pass-through properties, error handling and dead-letter queues, type mappings, and the supported targets.
    Bookshop lab: Oracle `BOOKSHOP.BOOK` → PostgreSQL `legacy_book` staging table. Mermaid: source topic → JDBC sink → upsert.
    Source: `B/connectors/jdbc.html` (#jdbc-consume-complex-debezium-events, #jdbc-at-least-once-delivery,
    #jdbc-primary-key-handling, #jdbc-delete-mode, #jdbc-idempotent-writes, #jdbc-schema-evolution,
    #jdbc-quoting-case-sensitivity, #jdbc-error-handling-and-dead-letter-queues, #jdbc-data-and-type-mappings,
    #jdbc-connector-properties, #jdbc-monitoring, #jdbc-faq), the `sqlserver-to-oracle` and `unwrap-smt` examples.
25. **`mongodb-sink-connector.adoc` — MongoDB Sink Connector.** Relational → document migrations (Bookshop reviews in the
    other direction), sink configuration, id strategies, and deletes. Source: `B/connectors/mongodb-sink.html`.
26. **`consuming-change-events-in-applications.adoc` — Listening to Change Events in Applications.** When a mapping is
    too complex for a sink connector (the legacy model ≠ the new model), the new application consumes the events itself:
    a Spring Boot 4.1 `@KafkaListener` that deserializes the Debezium envelope (JSON and Avro/Apicurio). Covers the
    anti-corruption layer translation (legacy `ORDERS` + `ORDER_LINE` rows → the `PurchaseOrder` aggregate), idempotency
    (source LSN/SCN + `ON CONFLICT`), ordering per key, out-of-order protection with the source position, handling
    tombstones, and the transaction metadata topic for assembling multi-row transactions. The same consumer is also shown in
    Quarkus with SmallRye Reactive Messaging and with Kafka Streams for aggregate building (DDD aggregates blog post). Links
    `spring-boot-kafka.adoc`, `kafka-consumers.adoc`, `kafka-streams.adoc`. Fig:
    `database-migration-anti-corruption-stream.svg`. Sources: the event pages of each connector, `B/integrations/serdes.html`.
27. **`debezium-engine.adoc` — Debezium Engine (Embedded).** Running a connector inside a Java application with no Kafka:
    the `DebeziumEngine` builder, the change event formats (JSON, Avro, CloudEvents, Connect), the offset and schema history
    stores (`B/configuration/storage.html`: File, Memory, JDBC, Redis, S3, Azure Blob, RocketMQ, Kafka), batch handlers and
    committing offsets, and when this is enough for a migration (a single consumer, a short migration). Also covers the Quarkus
    Debezium engine extension. Code: a complete Java 21 class that writes to PostgreSQL. Sources:
    `B/development/engine.html`, `B/integrations/quarkus-debezium-engine-extension.html`, `B/configuration/storage.html`.
28. **`debezium-server.adoc` — Debezium Server: Streaming Without Kafka.** Standalone Debezium configured with
    `application.properties` (`debezium.source.*`, `debezium.sink.*`, `debezium.format.*`, transforms, predicates). The
    sinks: Kafka, Kinesis, Pub/Sub, Pub/Sub Lite, HTTP, Pulsar, Event Hubs, Redis Streams, NATS Streaming and JetStream,
    Apache Fluss, Pravega, Infinispan, RocketMQ, RabbitMQ (stream and native stream), Milvus, Qdrant, InstructLab, JDBC,
    Iceberg, Databricks Zerobus. Explains how to pick a sink for a migration that runs on cloud messaging instead of Kafka.
    Lab: Oracle → Debezium Server → RabbitMQ stream → Spring consumer (links `backend/messaging/spring-boot-rabbitmq.adoc`),
    and Debezium Server + JDBC sink for Kafka-less replication (`data-replication` example). Source:
    `B/operations/debezium-server.html` (#debezium-server-<sink>-sink-configuration anchors).

### Schema changes during a migration

29. **`schema-changes-during-migration.adoc` — Handling Schema Changes.** What happens when the legacy schema changes
    while CDC is running. Covers the schema history topic (`schema.history.internal.kafka.topic`; required by
    MySQL/Oracle/SQL Server/Db2, not used by PostgreSQL/MongoDB) and recovering it, schema change events and topics
    (`include.schema.changes`), DDL parsing limits, SQL Server capture instances, PostgreSQL publications for new tables,
    JDBC sink `schema.evolution`, registry compatibility, and coordinating with Liquibase/Flamingock changes on the new
    side (expand/contract, linking `database/schema-evolution/best-practices.adoc`). Mermaid: an `ALTER TABLE` flowing from
    the legacy DB through the history topic to the sink. Sources: `#mysql-schema-history-topic`,
    `#sqlserver-schema-history-topic`, `#sqlserver-schema-evolution`, `B/transformations/schema-change-event-filter.html`,
    `#jdbc-schema-evolution`.

### Migration runbook (Bookshop end to end)

30. **`worked-example-oracle-to-postgresql.adoc` — Worked Example: Bookshop from Oracle to PostgreSQL.** A complete
    Docker Compose stack (Oracle Free, Kafka 4 KRaft, Debezium Connect 3.7.1.Final, Apicurio Registry, PostgreSQL 18, the new
    Spring Boot `bookshop`). Steps: prepare Oracle, register the Oracle source, run the initial snapshot, add JDBC sinks for
    the 1:1 tables, add the Spring consumer for the remodelled aggregates, generate legacy traffic with a script, watch lag,
    and verify. Every file is shown in full. Fig: `database-migration-bookshop-stack.svg`. Sources: the connector, sink and
    tutorial pages above, and the `debezium-examples` repo.
31. **`verification-and-reconciliation.adoc` — Verifying and Reconciling the Migrated Data.** How to prove that the new
    database matches the legacy one: row counts and per-chunk checksums (SQL for Oracle and PostgreSQL), sampling, a
    comparison job driven by the CDC position, end-to-end lag from `source.ts_ms`, `MilliSecondsBehindSource`, a parallel run of
    read paths behind feature flags (links the architecture page § Feature flags), and repairing drift with ad hoc incremental
    snapshots plus `additional-conditions`. Sources: `B/operations/monitoring.html`, `B/configuration/signalling.html`.
32. **`cut-over-and-reverse-replication.adoc` — Cut-over, Reverse Replication and Rollback.** Runbook for the read
    cut-over and then the write cut-over: drain lag to zero, the switch moment (a short write freeze, or per-aggregate/cohort
    routing behind the strangler proxy), then start **reverse CDC** (PostgreSQL connector → JDBC sink or a consumer → legacy
    Oracle) so that the legacy system stays current for rollback and for read-only legacy reports. Covers preventing loops in
    two-way sync (an origin column/marker, filtering on `source` metadata with the Filter SMT, separate users per direction),
    conflicts, and the point of no return. Decommissioning: drop connectors, slots, publications and supplemental logging,
    archive the topics. Fig: `database-migration-reverse-replication.svg`. Mermaid: the cut-over sequence. Sources:
    `B/transformations/filtering.html`, `B/connectors/postgresql.html`, `B/connectors/jdbc.html`, the Strangler Fig talk.

### Operations

33. **`running-on-kubernetes.adoc` — Running Debezium on Kubernetes: Strimzi, the Debezium Operator and the Platform.**
    Covers Strimzi `KafkaConnect` with the `build` section (adding the Debezium plugins and Oracle driver), `KafkaConnector` CRs,
    secrets via `KubernetesSecretConfigProvider`, the Debezium Operator (Helm install, the `DebeziumServer` CR), the
    **Debezium Management Platform** (connections, sources, destinations, transforms, pipelines), and OpenShift notes.
    Links `backend/kubernetes/*`. Sources: `B/operations/kubernetes.html`, `B/operations/openshift.html`,
    `B/operations/debezium-operator.html`, `B/operations/debezium-platform.html`, the Strimzi deploying/configuring docs.
34. **`monitoring-logging-and-tracing.adoc` — Monitoring, Logging and Tracing.** The JMX MBeans (snapshot, streaming and
    schema history metrics per connector), the Prometheus JMX exporter and the official Grafana dashboards (`monitoring`
    example), the JFR events, logging configuration and changing log levels at runtime, OpenTelemetry tracing across
    source → Kafka → consumer, and OpenLineage lineage. Lists the alerts that matter in a migration (lag, `QueueRemainingCapacity`,
    slot/WAL size, connector task FAILED). Links `database/prometheus/*` and `backend/messaging/kafka-operations-and-monitoring.adoc`.
    Sources: `B/operations/monitoring.html`, `B/operations/logging.html`, `B/integrations/tracing.html`,
    `B/integrations/openlineage.html`, `#postgresql-monitoring`, `#mysql-monitoring`.
35. **`offsets-restarts-and-exactly-once.adoc` — Offsets, Restarts and Exactly-Once.** Where offsets live (the Connect
    offsets topic, or other stores via `B/configuration/storage.html`), inspecting and resetting offsets (Connect REST
    `PATCH/DELETE /connectors/{name}/offsets`), re-running a snapshot safely, topic auto-creation
    (`topic.creation.*`, `B/configuration/topic-auto-create-config.html`), and exactly-once source support (`B/configuration/eos.html`)
    with the Kafka requirements. Links `kafka-reliability-and-exactly-once.adoc`.
36. **`troubleshooting-and-failure-recovery.adoc` — Troubleshooting and Failure Recovery.** A symptom → cause → fix
    table built from the FAQ and the "when things go wrong" sections: WAL/disk growth from idle slots, binlog purged
    before it was read, a lost Oracle archive log, an invalid MongoDB resume token, a corrupted schema history, a connector
    stuck in snapshot, slow LogMiner sessions, large transactions, and DB failover (PostgreSQL failover slots, MySQL GTIDs,
    the `failover` example). Error tolerance and DLQs for sinks. Sources: https://debezium.io/documentation/faq/,
    `#postgresql-when-things-go-wrong`, `#oracle-frequently-asked-questions`, `#connector-error-invalid-resume-token`,
    `#jdbc-faq`.
37. **`security-and-data-protection.adoc` — Security and Data Protection.** Least-privilege users per connector, TLS to
    the DB and to Kafka, secrets through config providers (file, Kubernetes, Vault), not migrating sensitive data
    (`column.exclude.list`, `column.mask.with.length.chars`, `column.mask.hash.*`, `column.truncate.to.length.chars`),
    topic ACLs, and the PII considerations of change history kept in Kafka (retention, compaction). Links
    `backend/messaging/kafka-security.adoc`. Sources: the connector property tables of each connector.
38. **`testing-cdc-pipelines.adoc` — Testing CDC Pipelines.** Integration tests with `debezium-testing-testcontainers`
    (`DebeziumContainer`, registering a connector, asserting on events), with Spring Boot 4.1 `@ServiceConnection`, and with
    an embedded Engine. Tests for the anti-corruption mapping and for idempotent replays. Links
    `backend/messaging/spring-boot-testing-messaging.adoc`. Sources: `B/integrations/testcontainers.html`, the
    `testcontainers` example.
39. **`cloud-and-managed-services.adoc` — Debezium with Cloud Databases and Managed Kafka.** Source settings for Amazon RDS /
    Aurora (PostgreSQL `rds.logical_replication`, MySQL binlog retention via `mysql.rds_set_configuration`, RDS Oracle
    LogMiner grants via `rdsadmin`), Cloud SQL (`cloudsql.logical_decoding`), and Azure Database for PostgreSQL / MySQL and
    Azure SQL. Running the connectors on Amazon MSK Connect, Confluent Cloud custom connectors or self-managed Connect on
    EKS/GKE/AKS, and the Red Hat build of Debezium (capabilities only, no prices). Links `cloud/aws/*` and
    `cloud/google-cloud/*`. Sources: `#postgresql-in-the-cloud`, the MySQL page, and the official cloud provider docs (add them to the bibliography).
40. **`other-uses-of-change-events.adoc` — Beyond Migration: Other Uses of Change Events.** A short page on the other
    official use cases that follow naturally once CDC is in place: cache invalidation (the Hibernate cache integration),
    audit logs, CQRS read models and search indexes (links `choosing-the-right-database.adoc`), and **Debezium AI**
    (embeddings, Docling, PyDebeziumAI; links `ai/rag-systems/ingestion-pipelines-and-freshness.adoc`). Sources:
    `B/integrations/hibernate-cache.html`, `B/ai/embeddings.html`, `B/ai/docling.html`, `B/ai/debezium-ai-python.html`,
    https://debezium.io/why/use-cases/, the audit-log and CQRS blog posts.

### Wrap-up

41. **`choosing-a-deployment-for-your-migration.adoc` — Choosing a Deployment for Your Migration.** A decision guide
    with a flowchart (Mermaid) and a table: Kafka Connect vs Debezium Server vs the Engine; JDBC sink vs an application
    consumer; snapshot strategy by data size; one-way vs two-way sync. Each row links to the page that covers it.
42. **`best-practices.adoc` — Best Practices.** A checklist for the whole migration, from preparation to decommission: one
    connector per source DB, `topic.prefix` naming, keys and the `REPLICA IDENTITY`, heartbeats, idempotent sinks, monitoring
    before go-live, rehearsing the cut-over and the rollback, and capacity planning. Each item links back to the page that
    explains it.
43. **`glossary.adoc` — Glossary.** CDC, LSN, SCN, GTID, binlog, WAL, replication slot, publication, oplog, resume token,
    envelope, tombstone, SMT, offset, schema history, snapshot (initial/incremental/blocking), signal, watermark, sink,
    strangler fig, anti-corruption layer, reverse replication. Each term links to its page.
44. **`cheat-sheet.adoc` — Cheat Sheet (PDF).** A one-page colour-coded summary + `xref:attachment$database-migration-cheat-sheet.pdf[...]`.
    Boxes: (1) migration phases and the source of truth in each; (2) the event envelope and `op` codes; (3) DB prerequisites
    for Oracle / PostgreSQL / MySQL / SQL Server / MongoDB (one line each); (4) a minimal source connector JSON; (5)
    `snapshot.mode` values + incremental snapshot signal SQL; (6) JDBC sink essentials (`insert.mode=upsert`,
    `primary.key.mode=record_key`, `delete.enabled`, `schema.evolution`); (7) key SMTs (ExtractNewRecordState,
    EventRouter, Filter, topic routing); (8) Connect REST commands (`POST /connectors`, `GET .../status`,
    `PUT .../pause`, `/restart`, offsets endpoints); (9) the metrics to watch; (10) the cut-over checklist; (11) the 3.7
